content:
You are assisting a physical therapist / physiatrist by drafting the objective findings and interpretation section of a clinical gait analysis report, based strictly on quantitative EMG and kinematic data extracted from an instrumented gait analysis. You are NOT diagnosing the patient and you are NOT recommending treatment.

Rules:
- Base every statement only on the numeric findings provided. Do not invent muscles, joints, or values not present in the input.
- If a finding is ambiguous or the data is insufficient to interpret confidently, say so explicitly rather than guessing.
- Use standard gait-analysis terminology (e.g., "prolonged activation", "delayed onset", "co-contraction", "reduced range of motion").
- Do not suggest specific treatments, exercises, or interventions.

Structure your output in exactly these sections:
1. Objective Findings — a factual restatement of the key numeric findings.
2. Muscle Activation Pattern — interpretation of onset/offset timing, amplitude, and co-contraction findings relative to normative gait.
3. Gait Deviation Summary — interpretation of the kinematic / composite deviation score findings.
4. Areas for Further Clinical Assessment — findings that warrant closer clinical examination, phrased as questions/flags, not conclusions.

Here are the quantitative gait analysis findings for one patient. Draft the report described in the system instructions.

Metric definitions (read before interpreting any number below):
- All joint angles and ROM values are SAGITTAL PLANE only. Coronal/transverse data are not included.
- EMG curves are ensemble averages of per-cycle envelopes, each cycle normalized to that subject's own per-muscle maximum before averaging. Amplitudes are therefore relative within-muscle values -- they are NOT absolute activation, force, or strength, and must not be compared across muscles as "stronger/weaker".
- Activation intervals are the regions where the averaged envelope exceeds 20% of that curve's own peak, minimum retained interval 3% of the cycle (by sample count). An interval written as (X%-Y%) with X > Y wraps across the 100%->0% cycle boundary (activity continuous across the cycle-defining event). An onset of 0% is the analysis-window boundary, not necessarily a physiological onset. "No interval detected" means no region met the threshold + duration criteria; it does NOT mean the muscle is inactive or non-functional.
- CCI is the Falconer-Winter co-contraction index computed on the full continuous envelopes (2*common area / summed areas), so it can be non-zero even when the DETECTED burst intervals of the pair do not overlap (sub-threshold activity contributes).
- The composite kinematic deviation score is the RMS of the per-joint Gait Variable Scores over the sagittal channels provided ("GPS-like", not the validated 9-variable GPS).
- Step length symmetry index: 200*(paretic - non-paretic)/(paretic + non-paretic), in %. NEGATIVE means the paretic-side step is SHORTER. Two operational step-length definitions exist (successive-footfall: each heel's position at its own initial contact; instantaneous: both heels at the same instant) and give different values for some subjects -- the definition actually used is stated next to the symmetry value.
- "Max |z| deviation" is the LARGEST absolute z-score across all 1001 phase points of the cycle, comparing this curve to the healthy-cohort mean/SD at each phase. This is an extreme-value statistic, NOT a single-observation z-score: in this dataset every one of 109 healthy controls exceeds |z| = 2 on at least one muscle, and per-muscle healthy 95th percentiles for this statistic run 3.65 (ERS) to 4.61 (TA) -- higher still under leave-one-out. Do not label a value abnormal by the conventional 2-SD rule; use the healthy reference range given per muscle where provided.
- Healthy-cohort CCI reference (this dataset): RF-vs-BF median 0.68 (2.5th-97.5th pct 0.48-0.83); TA-vs-GAS median 0.39 (0.24-0.59). Composite score reference: median 5.1, 95th percentile 10.7.
- COHORT BACKGROUND (calibration context, not necessarily the exact reference used for this subject -- the actual reference composition is stated in a dedicated line with the subject data below): the full healthy cohort is 138 subjects for kinematics, effective n = 106-109 per muscle for EMG (29 controls have no usable EMG; completeness varies by age), pooling both body sides and all ages; it is not age- or speed-matched to this subject. A leave-one-out run uses one subject fewer than these counts.
- SPEED SUPPORT LIMIT (applies to most stroke subjects in this dataset): the healthy reference cohort's self-selected walking speeds span 0.80-1.79 m/s. If this subject's gait speed is below 0.80 m/s, NO speed-matched healthy reference exists in this dataset -- 41 of the 50 stroke subjects are below that floor. Deviations from the reference then conflate slow-walking effects with stroke-specific control changes, and the two cannot be separated from these data. Describe deviations from the reference as such; do not attribute them wholly to stroke pathology.
- Fields NOT included in this summary but existing in the source dataset (deliberately out of scope for this version, not missing from the data): age, sex, time post-stroke, clinical scores (FAC/POMA/TIS), non-paretic-side curves, per-subject toe-off timing. Do not state that such information "does not exist" -- say it was not provided. Where a finding is absent because no interval met detection criteria or a channel is missing, that specific reason is stated inline.

Subject: Sub05_P (group: stroke, affected side: paretic)
Gait speed: 0.14 m/s (household ambulator (<0.4 m/s))
Cadence: 45.1 steps/min
Step length symmetry index: -23.1% (step-length definition: successive_footfall)
Composite kinematic deviation score (GPS-like): 14.22
Deviation reference actually used for this subject: 138 healthy subjects (pooled), 1001 phase points, source: main_cohort_excel.

Muscle activation findings:
- GAS: activation interval(s) 92%-88% (wraps cycle boundary), 97% of cycle above threshold, active across cycle boundary, peak normalized amplitude 0.39, max |z| vs healthy reference: 13.3 (above reference, at 80% of cycle)
- RF: activation interval(s) 86%-78% (wraps cycle boundary), 95% of cycle above threshold, active across cycle boundary, peak normalized amplitude 0.41, max |z| vs healthy reference: 3.3 (below reference, at 6% of cycle)
- VL: activation interval(s) 6%-69%; 97%-3% (wraps cycle boundary), 70% of cycle above threshold, active across cycle boundary, peak normalized amplitude 0.47, max |z| vs healthy reference: 5.3 (below reference, at 5% of cycle)
- BF: activation interval(s) 51%-64%; 65%-86%; 90%-51% (wraps cycle boundary), 95% of cycle above threshold, active across cycle boundary, peak normalized amplitude 0.42, max |z| vs healthy reference: 3.4 (above reference, at 29% of cycle)
- ST: activation interval(s) 48%-51%; 51%-47% (wraps cycle boundary), 99% of cycle above threshold, active across cycle boundary, peak normalized amplitude 0.50, max |z| vs healthy reference: 7.0 (above reference, at 35% of cycle)
- TA: activation interval(s) 39%-42%; 43%-77%; 83%-96%, 53% of cycle above threshold, peak normalized amplitude 0.24, max |z| vs healthy reference: 4.6 (below reference, at 0% of cycle)
- ERS: activation interval(s) 0%-100%, 100% of cycle above threshold, active across cycle boundary, peak normalized amplitude 0.35, max |z| vs healthy reference: 2.5 (below reference, at 2% of cycle)

Co-contraction indices:
- TA_vs_GAS: CCI = 0.50
- RF_vs_BF: CCI = 0.81

Joint kinematic findings (sagittal plane):
- AnkleAngles: range of motion 13.4 deg, Gait Variable Score 12.53
- KneeAngles: range of motion 43.2 deg, Gait Variable Score 22.24
- HipAngles: range of motion 25.7 deg, Gait Variable Score 12.32
- PelvisAngles: range of motion 4.8 deg, Gait Variable Score 2.33
